compiled_state.title: [CI llm-review concurrency]: cancel-in-progress cadence on rapid pushes -> review feedback only surfaces on final commit, blocking incremental review
compiled_state.author: Test
compiled_state.description:
### 1. Technical Environment

* **code_version:** worktree-20260506-183119 HEAD; PR #65
* **Discovered:** 2026-05-07 during sustained autonomous bug-fix session committing 11+ fixes onto a single PR branch.

### 2. Incident Overview

* **Scenario Type:** Sub-Agent Blocker

#### Expected Behavior

When an autonomous (or interactive) agent commits a sequence of fixes on a branch backing an open PR, the CI llm-review pass on each push should produce useful review feedback that the agent can address. The default CI cadence should let at least one full review complete per "logical batch" of commits so the agent sees actionable findings, not just cancellations.

#### Actual Behavior

CI runs on PR #65 were repeatedly cancelled mid-flight by the next push from the same branch. Observed sequence:

1. Push commit A → CI run 25476783436 starts (~10 min total)
2. ~3 min later: push commit B (an unrelated fix on the same branch) → run 25476783436 CANCELLED, run 25477389272 starts
3. ~5 min later: push commit C → run 25477389272 CANCELLED, ...

Net effect over 11 commits: only the last run produced findings; intermediate runs were cancelled before llm-review even started, so feedback that would have surfaced during commit 3 didn't arrive until commit 11. Several "real" findings (e.g., the dispatch.py canonical-prompt issue, the ticket-lib-api duplication) could have been addressed earlier and incrementally.

Concurrency control on push-driven workflows in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` is doing exactly what it's configured to do — cancel-in-progress on new push to the same ref. The friction is at the workflow design level: there's no batching, no debounce, and no "complete the current run if it's >50% done" carve-out.

### 3. Action History

* User instructed the agent to commit-push autonomously. The cancel-by-default cadence meant several llm-review findings were only surfaced on the final pre-merge run, after my context window was significantly drained.

### 5. Skills and Workflows

* `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — concurrency configuration
* CI llm-review job design
* Agent guidance: COMMIT-WORKFLOW.md or session-orchestrator skill could advise "wait N minutes between pushes when an open PR is in flight, OR amend the previous commit, OR push a chain locally and force-push once."

#### Suggested fix scope

Either:
A. Add a debounce on the workflow trigger (no cancel-in-progress; queue pushes within 60s into a single run).
B. Update agent guidance: when iterating on a PR with an in-flight CI, prefer `git commit --amend` (single commit per logical fix-batch) followed by `git push --force-with-lease`, so each push replaces the prior in-flight run instead of accumulating cancellations.
C. Surface CI-cancelled-by-newer-push as a structured signal so the orchestrator can pace pushes.

NOTE: this bug requires intent-alignment investigation before fix. The cancel-in-progress concurrency setting is intentional for fast feedback on the LATEST commit; changing it to debounce-batch would slow down feedback for human contributors. The fix may belong in agent guidance (option B) rather than the workflow itself.
